title: Python SDK: streaming-safe response factories and retry-aware parsers
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Current Python SDK helpers for structured outputs focus on strict hydration to typed models (pydantic/dataclasses) but do not handle streaming chunks (partial JSON), backpressure scenarios, or retries that replay partial responses. This causes brittle client code when using streaming generation with structured outputs and makes retries produce duplicate/invalid partial state.
acceptance_criteria: A streaming-safe response factory that can incrementally parse chunked JSON/NDJSON and emit fully hydrated typed objects when complete
Parse pipeline tolerates transient partial chunks, resumes seamlessly on retry without double-applying state
Provides ergonomic developer API: context manager for stream consumption, a simple 'hydrate' function that returns either dataclass or pydantic model depending on project config
Comprehensive unit and integration tests covering chunk boundaries, out-of-order keys, retry/reconnect, and malformed chunks
Documentation examples: short snippet for sync and async streaming usage and migration notes from current helpers
implementation_notes: Introduce ResponseFactory abstraction with two modes: incremental_parse (yields partial parse events) and finalize (returns model instance)
Use a small, dependency-free streaming JSON tokenizer (existing internal util or minimal parser) to avoid full-buffering
Design parse state that is idempotent and snapshot-able so retry paths can resume from last stable checkpoint or re-request from server without duplicate side-effects
Expose two high-level APIs: StreamHydrator (async iterator wrapper) and sync_stream context manager for blocking clients
Default model coercion to pydantic BaseModel; add opt-in dataclass conversion helper for teams preferring dataclasses
Keep kernel of parsing logic in a single module for easier backporting to TypeScript/Go SDKs
testing_plan: Unit tests: chunk boundary splits, escape sequences, nested objects, arrays, and NDJSON entries
Fuzz tests generating random chunk splits on representative model outputs to ensure parser stability
Integration tests against local dev server that simulates reconnects and mid-stream 500 responses to validate retry behavior
Performance microbench: measure latency and CPU overhead vs naive full-buffer parse for small/medium/large responses
Create a small example app (examples/structured_streaming_demo.py) used in CI smoke test to validate docs
Add contract tests asserting that hydrate(model, data) produces the same model instance when fed a complete payload or an equivalent stream of chunks
rollout_plan: Merge feature behind a feature flag 'streaming_hydrator' and enable for 10% of traffic in nightly builds
Collect telemetry: parse errors per 1k streams, average time-to-first-object, memory usage during stream parsing
If telemetry is healthy for 48h, increase to 50% and notify Demo/Docs teams to update examples
GA release as part of sdk-2025.04; provide migration guide and deprecation notes for older helpers

2025-02-15: Opted to snapshot parse state at object boundaries rather than token-level to reduce complexity for retries
